halloween event. film is flow, a reading from howl at halloween, facepainting, puzzles, colouring. cost €5 per person. all ages welcome. st join aidan byrne and fr sean jones for a special two-day retreat at the oratory of divine mercy in waterville on friday, 30th october, and saturday, 31st october . this retreat will offer a beautiful opportunity to deepen our faith , reflect on the communion of saints, and discover how we can help our dearly departed through prayer, the holy mass, and acts of devotion. friday, 30th october – beginning at 7:30pm the evening will begin with the rosary, followed by mass for the holy souls, a talk on all hallows eve, and concluding prayers for healing. saturday, 31st october – beginning at 9:30am. the day will include the rosary and talks on:‘our friends, the holy souls’ / ‘praying for the holy souls’ ‘blockag es to prayer’ ‘how the holy souls help their benefactors’ the retreat will culminate in mass for the holy souls at 3:00pm, fo llowed by healing prayers. all are warmly welcome to attend this special time o f prayer, reflection, and spiritual renewal. no charge but donations are welco me on the day. bring a packed lunch.⛳ congratulations to all ‘birdies for buddy’ a sincere word of congratulations and appreciation to everyone involved in the recent ‘birdies for buddy’ fundrais er, held at waterville golf links on saturday last. the day was truly blessed with beautiful sunshine, making it a wonderful occa sion filled with goodwill, generosity and community spirit. it was hea rtening to see so many people come together in support of this very worthy cause, raising funds for buddy and his pals at st francis special school in beaufort. a special word of thanks and appreciation to michael, miriam and all the team at waterville golf links for their generosity in making this wonderful event possible. their cont inued support for our community, and their kindness towards those in n eed, is greatly appreciated and is a wonderful example of the diffe rence we can make when we come together for others. to everyone who organised, participated in, sponsor ed and supported the fundraiser in any way, thank you. your generosity will make a real difference to buddy and his friends, and your support is a testament to the kindness and compassion that exists within our community. mass of remembrance for our deceased 25/26 friday 13th november: st finian’s 7.30pm one of the most cherished moments in our parish calendar is annual mass of remembrance for those who have died during the past year. we will gather in prayer for all our parishioners and loved ones who haved ied during 2025 and 2026, remembering their lives, giving thanks for the gifts they shared with us, and entrusting them to the loving mercy of god. this mass will be an opportunity for families and friends to come together in faith, to find comfort in the eucharist, and to remember those whose absence is still deeply felt. please contact the parish office to include names of those who died outside of the parish that you would like included in our mass. in november we remember as we welcome the month of november, the church invites us to turn our hearts in a special way towards the holy souls and to remember with love and gratitude all those who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith. november is a month of quiet reflection, heartfelt prayer and christian hope. we remember our parents, grandparents, relatives, friends, parishioners and all those whose lives have touched our own. though they are no longer with us in this earthly life, the bonds of love remain , and we continue to entrust them to the mercy and goodness of god. the church reminds us that death does not have the final word. through the death and resurrection of jesus christ, we are given the promise of etern al life. as we pray for the faithful departed, we are united with them in the communion o f saints, trusting that god's love is greater than death itself. “eternal rest grant unto them, o lord, and let perpetu al light shine upon them. may they rest in peace. amen.” the holy souls preparing for 30 days helping our dearly departed retreat at the oratory of divine mercy november lists of the dead during november, holy masses and prayers will be offered for all those remembered on our november lists of the dead, as we commend our departed loved ones to the loving mercy of god. parishioners are invited to place their lists in the offertory during mass or return them to the parish office throughout the month. we are deeply grateful for your prayerful remembrance and offering. date for the diary blessing of the oratory of the divine mercy friday 6 november 11:00am th by bishop ray browne - bishop of kerry more details in next week’s newsletter dromod/waterville

today’s celebration: we are called to love god and our neighbour: friend, visitor and stranger alike. penitential rite let us call to mind times we have failed to show love, remembering that god never fails to love and forgive us i confess … prayer your love, o god, is boundless. we who were strangers have been made your children. we who were defenceless have been brought into your household. keep us mindful of your deeds of mercy, that we may love you with our whole heart and love our neighbour as ourselves. we ask this through our lord jesus christ, your son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the holy spirit, god for ever and ever. introduction to the scripture readings 1st reading the people of israel are re-minded that in bad times they depended on the kindness of strangers. they should there-fore treat the weak and helpless with com-passion. 2nd. reading paul praises the people of salonika for their good christian living, which they had learned from him. the gospel jesus discloses the greatest commandment — love of god and neigh- bour. seeing your life though the lens of the gospel mt 22:34-40 1. you may feel some sympathy with the jews struggling to cope with 613 laws and wondering which were the important ones. have you ever felt overwhelmed by the rules and regulations of your own tradition? and have you ever been blessed by meeting someone, or reading something, that was able to cut through all the layers and point out to you what is essential in life? who was that person? what dids/he say or do? is there some phrase or text that encapsulates such wisdom for you? 2. if you were asked what is most important in life, what would your answer be? recall the experiences and relationships you have had. which are the ones that you treasure most? what
